b: NASHVILLE — In August 2026, a new event made its debut at Nashville’s Music City Center: WVC Nashville. The conference expanded upon the well-established WVC Vegas brand from Viticus Group, which serves veterinary professionals, and exceeded expectations for its inaugural year.

To find out more about Viticus Group’s launch of WVC Nashville, Trade Show Executive (TSE) connected with Joyce Goedeke, Senior Director of Marketing and Communications at Viticus Group, to talk 2026 outcomes, marketing learnings and plans for 2027.
In year one of WVC Nashville, the show saw more than 8,800 participants and sold 170,000 net square feet of exhibits.

“We were pleased to welcome a strong number of participants to WVC Nashville within the Nashville and Tennessee drive markets,” Goedeke said. “We experienced increased participant numbers from surrounding states that do not consistently participate at WVC Vegas, as well as experiencing nearly 55% of first-time participants at WVC Nashville. It was wonderful to welcome nearly 600% more participants from Tennessee to WVC Nashville than those who attend WVC Vegas.”
The 2027 edition will see the event expand to take over the entirety of Music City Center.

“We anticipate the growth at WVC Nashville will be rapid; however, we want to ensure that doesn’t take away from what people described as a large conference that feels intimate. We do believe we could hit 10,000-plus attendees in year two with steady growth each year moving forward as the word gets out to our friends on the East Coast,” Goedeke said.

According to TSE’s 2026 World’s Top Convention Centers Directory, Nashville’s Music City Center features 353,000 sf of prime exhibit space and another 90,000 sf of meeting space alongside 75,400 sf of flex space. The LEED Gold Certified facility also offers 60 breakout rooms and 2 large ballrooms.
Finding Opportunity in a New Region
While Viticus Group’s flagship WVC Vegas event is bringing the animal health industry together annually, the team identified a market gap that led to the creation of the new launch.

“Confidence in the Nashville market stemmed from years of demand in Vegas and a clear need to make specialized, hands-on continuing education more accessible to East Coast and Southeast veterinary and human health professionals,” Goedeke said. “The expansion was in discussion for several years by past and current executive leadership and the Board of Directors. Timing, extensive research, strategic planning and courage all contributed to the expansion’s reality.”

Viticus Group also realized they needed to expand accessibility to training and products in a new place to reach professionals who could not attend the Q1 Vegas show due to budgeting, staffing or other obstacles at that time of year.

The new event provided more choices to professionals on where and how to get their education, and the market responded accordingly. According to the audience data from WVC Nashville, a majority of the attendees were first-timers to a Viticus Group event.
By holding the Nashville event in Q3 of the year, Viticus Group was able to capitalize on the sense of urgency the industry had around using their continuing education budgets by the year’s end.

For the WVC Nashville event, the Viticus Group team knew it needed to deliver the same experiences the brand is known for, while ensuring expectations were in check for those coming to the new launch.

“Our team was deliberate in structuring the marketing around WVC Nashville-launched experiential learning, highlighting the accessibility of a new conference and purpose-built hands-on training facilities in our second home, while leveraging the Music City culture to differentiate the event from its Vegas sibling,” Goedeke said.
Using data to drive decision-making and marketing efforts, the team saw real results from campaigns.

“FOMO works. We executed a variety of strategies to highlight who was attending the show,” Goedeke said. “Between attendees and executives, we saw a major increase within the last 60 days of the event, and we believe our messaging was a big part of it.”

The team also found that surprise-and-delight experiences throughout the event generated some of the most memorable moments for attendees, reinforcing their belief that those experiences are essential to WVC events and often supported by sponsors.

Knowing that Nashville was going to be the epicenter for this new event, Viticus Group invested in permanent, purpose-built buildings mirroring its Vegas Education Centers to conduct training: the Viticus Group Nashville Centers. The Education Centers span two buildings and feature 80,000 sf of training facilities that make specialized, hands-on continuing education more accessible to East Coast and Southeast veterinary and human health professionals.

The facility brings another layer to the WVC Nashville programming with true real-world environments, and creates a complementary experience to the WVC Vegas event where the organization also has purpose-built spaces.

“Having access to our state-of-the-art education centers in conjunction to our WVC conferences are part of what sets us apart from any other veterinary conference in the world,” Goedeke said. “In addition, choosing a city that people want to visit repeatedly was the primary driver and who doesn’t want to visit Nashville at least once a year, if not more?”

When the show is not taking place, Viticus Group holds year-round training programs and events, and also allows other groups, like medical device companies, to rent the space for continuing education and training events in animal and human health.
Building Momentum for a Centennial Celebration
The year 2028 marks the 100th anniversary of WVC Vegas, and the team is strategically harnessing momentum leading up to the milestone anniversary.

“We are positioned to utilize both conferences in 2027 to act as a gateway to the 100th anniversary in 2028 and expand our audience reach and awareness across the events versus isolating the reach to one location, one event,” Goedeke said.

“With our 100th anniversary, bringing full brand awareness to all of our services is a great place to bring the message home as we enter a new century of education,” she added. “WVC Vegas and WVC Nashville each offer a distinct mix of education and experiences, but both share a commitment to hands-on training that helps attendees return to practice with greater confidence. As WVC Vegas marks its 100th anniversary, we have an opportunity to introduce more people to the full range of what Viticus Group offers, from our WVC conferences to year-round training in veterinary and human health in Vegas and now Nashville.”
